transcript:
>> This is "NPR News Now," the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from "NPR News" in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
Maryland Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen says he will run
for Senate Majority Leader in the next Congress,
setting up a challenge to Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer
after the party swept to power in the midterm elections.
Van Hollen said in a statement that, quote,
"The American people called for change.
The race will be the first contested election
for Democratic Leader in decades."
>> President Trump's son Donald Jr.
is out at the prediction market, Kalshi.
As NPR's Luke Garrett reports, he was an advisor to the company,
which saw explosive growth
and little regulation during Trump's presidency.
>> Prediction market Kalshi says the company
and the president's eldest son mutually agreed to part ways.
The stated reason, Donald Trump Jr.
made a significant investment
in Kalshi's top competitor, Polymarket.
The two prediction markets allow for users
to bet billions on elections, sports, and culture.
During Trump's second term, both Kalshi and Polymarket
have enjoyed little to no regulation
from its federal regulator,
the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
CFTC staffing and enforcement have fallen dramatically,
catching the attention of Capitol Hill Democrats
who have vowed to investigate the agency,
Kalshi, and Polymarket.
Donald Trump Jr.'s departure comes as tech companies
work to burnish their relationships with Democrats
who will retake control of Congress in January.
Luke Garrett, NPR News, Washington.
>> NVIDIA CEO Jensen Wong has resigned after reports
that he had extramarital affairs, including one
with a suspected Chinese spy.
NPR's John Ruich has more.
>> There's a lot we don't know about the spy allegations,
which NPR has not independently confirmed
and which China denies.
We don't know if any NVIDIA information
might have been compromised or national security,
for that matter.
The U.S. bans the export of NVIDIA's best chips to China,
so that's why allegations that Wong was involved with someone
who might have been a spy for China are so alarming.
Second, the company faces uncertainty.
You know, Jensen Wong was, by all accounts,
a micromanager.
He had his hand in loads of decisions at the company,
big and small.
Dozens of senior employees looked to him for direct guidance,
and Jensen Wong had no apparent succession plan.
>> NPR's John Ruich reporting, "Existing home sales
are at their lowest level in 16 years.
The National Association of Realtors
says sales last month were down nearly 9% from a year ago,
as NPR's Stephen Bissaha reports.
A large part of that's due to high mortgage rates."
>> Here's how Realtor.com senior economist
Joel Berner described October's housing market slope.
>> It was a punch in the gut.
We expected to see a soft month,
but not the softest month since 2010.
>> The gut punch came from mortgage rates peaking in October.
This week, the average rate for a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage
is 7.11%, down a bit,
but still well above the same time last year.
Berner does think if rates stabilize,
sales could pick up again next year.
>> The people who want to buy and the people who want to sell
are just waiting for a spring awakening in 2027.
>> But first, the housing market will likely have to sit
through another tough winter.
Stephen Bissaha, NPR News.
>> And from Washington, you're listening to NPR News.
Federal officials say there's new funding
to study the medical potential
of a powerful psychedelic ibogaine.
Ibogaine is made from an African plant
that can cause intense hallucinations,
nausea, tremors, and dangerous heart rhythms.
Veterans groups say it can help hard-to-treat conditions,
like PTSD, depression, and opioid addiction.
A widespread Microsoft service outage
impacted thousands of users today.
The tech giant base in Washington state
says it's working to get affected servers back in service,
but the outage caused some businesses to close for the day,
from member station KNKX in Seattle.
Anna-Marie Iani has more.
>> Outlook emails, Microsoft Teams messaging,
and other 365 services were affected.
Gary Renville runs the nonprofit Project Access Northwest.
His small team connects low-income patients
with health and dental care.
>> We actually had to shut down our business today
because of the outage.
I had to send my employees home.
>> He says without Teams and Outlook,
they didn't have a secure way to talk to patients.
>> It's about the real impact of somebody
who's been waiting for an appointment for months,
who might not have been able to get through to us.
>> Microsoft spent much of the day working on the outage,
saying they were pursuing, quote,
"all available pathways to restore service."
For NPR News, I'm Anna-Marie Iani in Seattle.
>> A lightsaber used by Darth Vader in the Empire Strikes Back
and Return of the Jedi sold for nearly $5 million
in an auction today.
According to Heritage Auctions,
the sale marks a world auction record
for any Star Wars collectible.
In July, Luke Skywalker's lightsaber
and severed hand prop from Empire Strikes Back
sold for $3.75 million. This is NPR.

topics.text: Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen announces run for Senate Majority Leader against Chuck Schumer
Donald Trump Jr. parts ways with prediction market Kalshi over investment in rival Polymarket
NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang resigns after reports of extramarital affairs, including with suspected Chinese spy
Existing home sales fall to lowest level in 16 years, down nearly 9% from last year
Federal officials announce new funding to study ibogaine's medical potential for PTSD and addiction
Widespread Microsoft service outage disrupts Outlook and Teams, forcing some Seattle businesses to close
Darth Vader's lightsaber from Empire Strikes Back sells for nearly $5 million at auction
